questions.text: Tell me a little bit about yourself.
What do you enjoy outside of work and school?
What is the last book you read?
What are you well known for?
Why do you want to be a PA for the rest of your working career?
How did you find out about the PA profession?
Have you considered medical school?
Explain the role of a PA to a patient.
What have you observed while shadowing?
If PAs made $20,000 a year, would you still want to be a PA?
What is appealing about the location of Duke's PA program?
Have you interviewed anywhere else?
If you are not accepted into this program, what do you think would be the reason?
There's one spot left and it's between you and another candidate. The other candidate has a higher GPA. Who should be chosen?
How do you plan on improving yourself if not accepted into PA school?
What would your co-workers say is your greatest weakness?
What would your last employer say about you?
Do you ever get angry or frustrated?
How has your background prepared you for the intense physical and mental rigor it takes to become a PA?
How would you feel in PA school if you were doing poorly in a subject that you excelled in during undergrad?
How do you study best?
Are you able to handle multiple assignments at once?
How would you describe your overall academic performance?
Who is going to support you through school?
What is a dependent practitioner, and how do you feel about practicing as one?
Are there laws you feel limit the PA profession unfairly?
What do you know about the history of the PA profession.
Would you accept a Facebook friend request from a patient?
Is there a specific specialty or ideal job you envision for yourself as a PA?
You are a PA. A patient on your schedule insists on seeing an MD. How do you handle it?
Describe your volunteer experience.
Discuss a time you had to communicate effectively under pressure.
Tell me about a situation when you had to push yourself.
Give an example of a situation in which you exceeded expectations.
Tell me about a time you disappointed someone.
Describe a disappointing moment from your life.
What is the worst mistake you have ever made?
Discuss an experience that allowed you to learn something important about yourself.
Tell me about a time you received negative feedback and how you used it to improve yourself.
Have you ever had to share bad news?
You are a PA. Your collaborating MD asks you to administer a medication to a patient. You do not agree with his decision and feel it could harm the patient. What do you do?

You have an elderly patient who needs to stay at the hospital for overnight observation. The patient is refusing, but the patient's son states the patient has dementia and is incapable of making medical decisions. The patient's son wants the patient admitted. What do you do?
A patient calls back for their culture results, and you realize the test was never sent in. The sample is no longer good. What do you do?

A child is brought in with injuries from falling out of a tree at a friend's house. His parents are out of town. After evaluation, it is determined that he requires a blood transfusion. Before giving the transfusion, you find a card in his pocket stating he is Jehovah's Witness and to not give blood transfusions. The procedure would save his life, but no parents are present. What do you do?
What would you do if you hit a car in a parking lot? You're unsure of the owner.

You are seeing a patient who is a gymnast and currently training for the Olympics. The patient's mother is upset because the patient recently gained 3 pounds. Enter the room and address this situation.
While sitting back to back, tell the person in the room how to draw a tree.
